findings.finding: The thresholds are overfit, and the input doc says so. input-improvements.md:18-19 picks 0.5 because on-target #1 had p 0.59-0.98 and off-target #1 had p 0.28-0.40, over 12 runs from 6 tasks (only 2 tasks are wrong). Any cut between 0.41 and 0.58 would separate them just as well, so 0.5 is an in-sample midpoint. The 0.9 cumulative and max-5 values have no supporting data at all. The planned check (doc line 23: low on exactly n5/n6) re-runs the same 6 tasks, so it cannot validate the threshold. Mark GATE as provisional in SKILL.md/the code comment and validate on held-out tasks before treating it as calibrated.
findings.resolution: accepted by the user for this run (2026-10-18), not fixed: marked PROVISIONAL in code and SKILL.md; the run re-measures the same 6 tasks, so it cannot calibrate the cut

findings.finding: The gate result is not written to runs.jsonl. The appendJsonl record has no gate/confidence/top1, although the design asked for `confidence` and `p1` in the log. The planned acceptance check ('check runs.jsonl: confidence low on exactly n5 and n6') therefore cannot be done from the log. It can only be rebuilt from jev.global.order[0].p, which is unclear after the gate itself was turned off with --no-gate.

The 0.5 threshold is applied to a probability whose meaning changes with the number of options. In the single-batch path, global.order comes from a pool of up to 24 options plus none. In the multi-batch path it comes from the survivor pass, typically keep*batches (about 8-16 options). Both include none_of_these mass, which is filtered out of the order but still takes probability. So the same 0.5 means different things depending on pool size, and the 12 calibration runs did not cover both paths in a controlled way.

The docstring contradicts the code. It says a 'Jev fallback/skip → low', but the code returns 'n/a' for fallback, skip and not-called runs. The code matches the stated intent (fallback prints as before); the comment is wrong.

The cumulative sum has a floating-point edge case: `cum >= g.cumulative`. For example 0.7+0.2 = 0.8999999999999999 < 0.9, so an extra row is shown. Fix with a small epsilon (cum >= g.cumulative - 1e-9).

The markdown does not say that rows were hidden in the high-confidence case, and it shows no p column. The design asked for a p column, and a LOW line telling the agent to 'search with new terms'. Neither the agent nor the user can see that 10 rows were cut to 1-5, or what each row's p is, unless they read SKILL.md. Suggest adding 'showing N of M (Jev p ...); --no-gate for all'.

--no-gate parsing works only when the flag is last or followed by another --flag. parseArgs (decision-provider.mjs:143) takes the next non-'--' token as the value. So `--no-gate false` gives the string 'false', which is truthy and turns the gate off, and a following positional argument would be swallowed. The flag is boolean-only, so this rarely matters, but it is not documented.

Tests cover confidenceGate and toMarkdown with hand-built objects only. Not covered: explore() wiring (result.gate present when Jev is called; gate:false gives n/a and all rows), the CLI `--no-gate` (spawnSync test, like the existing numeric-option test), the multi-batch global-pass path through jevRank with a mocked decide, --json still carrying full top plus gate, and the 0.5 boundary (top1 exactly 0.5 is high). The test helper gj also builds ids 'c0' instead of the candId format; harmless but not realistic.

When top1 >= 0.5 but none_of_these holds most of the remaining mass (e.g. p1 0.5, noneP 0.45, noneWon false), the result is 'high' but the cumulative sum over non-none rows never reaches 0.9, so it always prints maxRows (5) low-p rows. That is the opposite of the noise-cutting goal. Consider normalising over non-none mass, or treating a large noneP as low.

The LOW CONFIDENCE line and the later Jev status line both say that none_of_these won, so it is printed twice. Not a bug. The JSON output stays complete: r.top is not truncated, and gate.shown tells consumers how many rows to show. Wiring is correct: ord[0].p reads {id,p} from readBatch, r.top head order equals jev.global.order, and slice(0, shown) is safe when top is shorter. All 19 tests pass.
